title: Four Lists Joined
statement: Four non-empty lists of positive numbers all have the same sum. The means of the four lists are $30$, $40$, $60$ and $120$. The lists are joined to form one long list, with every entry of every list kept, including repeated values. What is the mean of the long list?
hints: Give the common sum of the four lists a name, say $S$. How many entries does the list with mean $30$ have, in terms of $S$?

Do not simply average the four means, because the lists have different lengths. Find the total of the long list and its length separately, each in terms of the common sum $S$, as is done when calculating a harmonic mean. A list with sum $S$ and mean $m$ has $\frac{S}{m}$ entries.

Let the common sum be $S$. The long list has sum $4S$ and length $\frac{S}{30} + \frac{S}{40} + \frac{S}{60} + \frac{S}{120}$. Over the common denominator $120$, this length simplifies to $\frac{S}{12}$. Now divide the sum by the length.
solution:
Let each list have sum $S>0$. A list with mean $m$ has $S/m$ entries, so the long list has sum $4S$ and length
$$S\left(\dfrac{1}{30}+\dfrac{1}{40}+\dfrac{1}{60}+\dfrac{1}{120}\right)=S\cdot\dfrac{4+3+2+1}{120}=\dfrac{S}{12}.$$
The mean is $\frac{4S}{S/12}=48$.
